trip: Mexico 2026 — Mexico City · Teotihuacán · Oaxaca (Día de Muertos)

meta.party: 2 adults, German passports, no car (buses, flights, taxis and one guided valley tour)
meta.route: Berlin (BER) → Mexico City ×4n → Oaxaca ×4n → Mexico City ×1n → Berlin
meta.self_check: self-checked: 8 issues found and fixed — (1) day 5 mixed an intercity flight with 3 anchors, the Zócalo/Santo Domingo block demoted to a free stroll; (2) Museo Frida Kahlo closes Mondays and sells no counter tickets, moved to Sat 31 Oct with a timed online slot on the checklist; (3) Museo Vivo del Muralismo closes Tuesdays — the Centro day sits on Thursday; (4) Museo Nacional de Antropología and Museo del Palacio de Bellas Artes both close Mondays, and the only Monday in the window (2 Nov) is spent in Oaxaca, so nothing collides; (5) the CDMX Día de Muertos parade date is NOT published for 2026 — day 4 was rebuilt so it works with or without it (swap tag + rain_alt); (6) day 3's Teotihuacán → Mercado de Jamaica return was two hop rows against one stop-pair and would have shifted every later map link, merged into one row; (7) departure day had the museum running to 13:30 against a 19:30 international departure — museum now hard-stops at 12:30 and the airport transfer carries a 3 h international buffer plus real traffic time; (8) day 8's Hierve el Agua has been closed by community disputes more than once, so it is tagged [skippable] and the tour is booked for the Mitla/Teotitlán half.

decisions: Round trip BER↔MEX, not open-jaw. Oaxaca (OAX) has no useful intercontinental service, so an open jaw would mean an OAX→MEX self-transfer on a separate ticket on departure day — the one shape that turns a missed domestic hop into a missed transatlantic flight. Cost of the decision: one night back in Mexico City on 5 Nov.

Oaxaca gets the Día de Muertos nights (1–2 Nov), Mexico City gets the parade weekend (31 Oct). The two cities peak on different days, so this is the rare case where you can have both: CDMX's Saturday desfile and Coyoacán ofrendas, then Oaxaca's 1 Nov comparsa and the 1–2 Nov cemetery vigils.

Fly CDMX↔Oaxaca, do not take ADO. ADO GL/Platino is 6.5–7 h each way and would eat a whole festival day in each direction; the flight is 1 h 05 and about 3 h 30 door to door. ADO stays on the page as the budget backup (and as the fallback if the 1 Nov flights price out) — it is comfortable, it is just slow.

Teotihuacán yes, Puebla no. Puebla is a good day but it would have cost either a Muertos night in Oaxaca or the Coyoacán day; Teotihuacán is 1 h out of the city and also feeds the mural interest (the Tepantitla Tlalocan wall paintings are inside the site).

2 Nov is deliberately half-empty in the afternoon. The day starts at the Abastos market at 09:00 and ends at a cemetery close to midnight; a normal three-anchor afternoon in between would have made the night unbearable.

No car at any point. The Tlacolula valley (Teotitlán del Valle · Mitla · mezcal) is done as a small-group guided tour, which is also the only way to see a working weaving workshop and a palenque without a rental.

checklist.item: Oaxaca hotel, 1–5 Nov (4 nights) — refundable if possible
checklist.deadline: TODAY. This is the single most time-critical line on the page.
checklist.price: €140–230/night for two on 1–2 Nov, €90–130 on 3–4 Nov
checklist.note: ⚠️ Guides written for the 2026 season say to book Oaxaca by May 2026 and that centro is largely gone by September, with rates 2–3× normal for 31 Oct – 2 Nov. Booking in mid-August means you are late: take Jalatlaco or the Santo Domingo fringe rather than holding out for the Zócalo.

checklist.item: MEX→OAX (1 Nov) and OAX→MEX (5 Nov) domestic flights
checklist.deadline: this week — 1 Nov is the single busiest domestic day of the Mexican year
checklist.price: ⚠️ MX$1,500–3,500 pp per leg at festival pricing — check, do not assume the €50 fares you see for a Tuesday in February
checklist.note: Aeroméxico (T2), Volaris and VivaAerobús (T1) all fly it. Check which terminal before booking the airport taxi. Backup: ADO GL from Terminal TAPO / Terminal Norte, ~6.5–7 h, MX$800–1,300 pp — book that on ado.com.mx, not a reseller.

checklist.item: Travel-medical insurance for two, WITH repatriation cover (Auslandsreise-Kranken- und Rückholversicherung)
checklist.deadline: the moment you book the flights
checklist.note: The Auswärtiges Amt is unusually blunt about this one: private hospitals in Mexico expect payment in cash on the spot, and consular assistance is billed back to the traveller. This is not the line to skip.

checklist.item: Museo Frida Kahlo (Casa Azul) timed ticket, Sat 31 Oct, 10:00 slot for two
checklist.deadline: as soon as the date opens — at minimum 1–2 weeks ahead
checklist.note: Online only — the museum no longer sells at the door, so turning up without a QR code means not going in. The ticket also covers Museo Diego Rivera Anahuacalli. Closed Mondays.

checklist.deadline: within 2–3 weeks; Muertos week is a demand peak on the Europe–Mexico market
checklist.price: €1,555–1,815 total for two, round trip (Google cache via flight_scan, 2026-08-15)
checklist.note: Every row in the cache was 2 stops. Also price the obvious 1-stop shape by hand — BER→FRA→MEX on Lufthansa — before you buy; the scanner did not surface it.

checklist.item: Mexico City hotel, 28 Oct – 1 Nov and 5–6 Nov (Roma Norte / Condesa)
checklist.deadline: 4–6 weeks out; re-shop 2–3 weeks before travel
checklist.note: Book the 5–6 Nov night as a separate reservation in the same hotel if you can — the same front desk on the way out is worth more than €10 of savings when you are leaving at 15:30 with luggage.

checklist.item: Tlacolula valley small-group tour, Wed 4 Nov (Tule · Teotitlán del Valle · Mitla · mezcal palenque)
checklist.deadline: 2–3 weeks out; free cancellation up to 24 h is standard
checklist.price: ≈ MX$900–1,400 pp including site fees and a comida
checklist.note: ⚠️ Confirm whether the itinerary depends on Hierve el Agua — access there has been shut by community disputes more than once. Take a tour that still runs Mitla and Teotitlán if it is closed.

checklist.item: Re-check the CDMX Desfile de Día de Muertos date and route
checklist.deadline: mid-September 2026, when the Secretaría de Cultura CDMX publishes it
checklist.note: ⚠️ Not published as of 2026-08-15. History says a Saturday in the window — 31 Oct or 7 Nov 2026. 7 Nov is one day after you fly home, so day 4 is written to be a good day either way.

checklist.item: Passports: 6 months' validity beyond entry; nothing else to file
checklist.deadline: check now — a renewal takes weeks
checklist.note: German passport = visa-free up to 180 days. Arriving by air there is NO paper FMM any more: entry is the digital FMMd, and biometric German passports can use the E-Gates at AICM. Do not buy an 'FMM tourist card' from a website — by air it does not exist.

checklist.item: eSIM for two + small cash float in pesos
checklist.price: ≈ €5–25 pp for 5–10 GB; withdraw MX$4,000–6,000 on arrival
checklist.note: Markets, cemeteries, colectivos, comparsa food stalls and tips are all cash. Restaurant tipping is 10–15%.

checklist.item: Re-confirm opening hours and fees two weeks before travel
checklist.note: INAH raised its fees on 1 January 2026 and can do it again; museum hours around 1–2 November shift locally every year. Everything on this page is a pattern verified 2026-08-15, not a date-specific confirmation.

Templo Mayor + site museum
timeline.price: ⚠️ MX$100–210 pp — INAH raised fees on 2026-01-01 and the flagship rate for foreign visitors is now MX$210; this site's own 2026 rate is unverified
timeline.note: Tue–Sun 09:00–17:00, last entry 16:30; closed Mondays (pattern as of 2026-08-15). Being first in means the Templo Mayor's stacked pyramids to yourself. The museum's Tlaltecuhtli monolith is the piece to make time for.

timeline.what: Walk · Templo Mayor → the SEP courtyards · 0.6 km · 10 min
Museo Vivo del Muralismo — the SEP courtyards
timeline.note: Diego Rivera's 235-panel cycle wraps two full courtyards of the Education Ministry — the largest single body of his mural work anywhere, and almost nobody is here. 10:00–18:00, closed Tuesdays and national holidays (pattern as of 2026-08-15).

timeline.what: Walk · SEP → Palacio de Bellas Artes · 1.3 km · 18 min, along Calle Tacuba
Museo del Palacio de Bellas Artes — the mural floor
timeline.price: MX$95 pp (+MX$30 per camera); free on Sundays
timeline.note: Tue–Sun 10:00–18:00, closed Mondays. Rivera's 'Man, Controller of the Universe' — the repainted Rockefeller Center mural — plus Siqueiros and Orozco on the same two floors. This is the densest muralism hour in Mexico.

timeline.what: Walk · Bellas Artes → Mercado de San Juan · 0.9 km · 12 min
Lunch · Mercado de San Juan — food area
timeline.note: The city's produce-and-delicatessen market rather than a tourist food hall: cheese and charcuterie counters that will build you a plate, plus a couple of seafood stalls at the back.

Museo Mural Diego Rivera
timeline.note: Built around one painting: 'Dream of a Sunday Afternoon in the Alameda Central', moved here after the 1985 earthquake. Tue–Sun 10:00–18:00.

days.ribbon: Roma Norte →taxi 35′→ Terminal Norte →bus 60′→ Teotihuacán Puerta 1 →bus+taxi 2 h 15→ Mercado de Jamaica →taxi 30′→ Roma Norte
days.rain_alt: Late October is the dry side of the year here (0.3 mm across the same ten days last year), but if it does break: the site's Museo de la Cultura Teotihuacana and the Tepantitla mural shelter are both roofed, and the Jamaica market is entirely under cover.

timeline.what: Taxi · Roma Norte → Terminal de Autobuses del Norte · ~11 km · 30-40 min · MX$180-250
Autobuses Teotihuacanos · Terminal Norte gate 8 → Teotihuacán Puerta 1 · ~1 h · ≈MX$60 pp
timeline.note: Departures roughly every 20 min from 06:00. Ask for 'Pirámides', not 'San Juan Teotihuacán' — the town bus drops you 3 km short.

timeline.what: Teotihuacán — Calzada de los Muertos, Pyramid of the Moon plaza, Palacio de Quetzalpapálotl
timeline.note: Open daily 09:00–17:00, last access 16:30 (2026 rate and pattern verified 2026-08-15). ⚠️ Climbing the Sun and Moon pyramids has been prohibited since 2020 — assume you are walking around them, not up them. Enter at Puerta 1 and walk north so the sun is behind you.

timeline.what: Tepantitla mural complex — the Tlalocan wall paintings
timeline.note: Ten minutes' walk east of the Pyramid of the Sun and the reason a mural-minded trip comes here: 1,500-year-old painted walls of a paradise garden, the ancestor of everything you saw yesterday on the SEP courtyards.

timeline.what: Lunch · the comedores at Puerta 1 / La Gruta cave restaurant — food area
timeline.note: La Gruta is in a lava cave beside Puerta 5 and takes reservations; the Puerta 1 comedores are a third of the price and perfectly good.

Mercado de Jamaica — the cempasúchil market
timeline.price: free; a bunch of marigolds MX$50–120
timeline.note: The city's flower market, open 24/7, and in the last week of October it turns into an orange canyon: cempasúchil by the tonne, plus copal, sugar skulls and papel picado for the ofrendas. Late afternoon is when the Muertos stalls are fully set and the light is best.

Museo Frida Kahlo · Casa Azul
timeline.note: Timed ticket, online only — no counter sales at all. Sat 10:00–18:00, closed Mondays (verified 2026-08-15). Book the 10:00 slot: the house is small and by noon it is a queue with a garden attached. Ticket also admits you to Museo Anahuacalli.

timeline.what: Desfile de Día de Muertos · Paseo de la Reforma
timeline.tag: swap→Museo Nacional de Antropología (10 min away) or the Mega Procesión de Catrinas, if the parade is not today
timeline.note: ⚠️ THE 2026 DATE IS NOT PUBLISHED. The parade has run on a Saturday in this window every year and 31 Oct 2026 is the likely one, with 7 Nov the alternative; the Secretaría de Cultura CDMX confirms 4–6 weeks out. Route runs Puerta de los Leones (Chapultepec) → Reforma → Av. Juárez → 5 de Mayo → Zócalo, roughly 12:00–16:00, ~6 km. Stand at the Ángel or the Glorieta de la Palma and be in place by 11:00 if you want a front row.

timeline.note: Check your terminal the night before: Aeroméxico is T2, Volaris and Viva are T1, and they are 3 km apart.

Taxi · Aeropuerto de Oaxaca → Hotel · Oaxaca centro · ~9 km · 25-35 min · MX$250-350 (or the shared colectivo van, MX$100 pp)
Drop bags, coffee on Alcalá
Walk · Hotel · Oaxaca centro → Mercado 20 de Noviembre · 0.8 km · 12 min
Mercado Benito Juárez + Mercado 20 de Noviembre — the Pasillo de Humo
timeline.price: MX$150–350 pp for lunch; chapulines and chocolate by weight
timeline.note: Open daily ~06:00–22:00 (verified 2026-08-15). In the Pasillo de Humo you are handed a tray of chiles and spring onions, you pick your meat at a stall, and it is grilled over charcoal in front of you — then you carry it to a table and buy tortillas, salsa and agua fresca from whoever walks past. On 1 November the surrounding aisles are pure Muertos: pan de muerto, chocolate for the atole, cempasúchil by the armful.

timeline.what: Zócalo · Catedral · Templo de Santo Domingo · the sand tapestries on Alcalá
timeline.note: An orientation stroll rather than an anchor — today is a moving day. The tapetes de arena laid outside the churches and courtyards are made and swept away within the week.

timeline.what: Rest at the hotel
timeline.note: Non-negotiable. Tonight ends after 22:00 and tomorrow starts at 09:00.

timeline.what: Early dinner · centro — food area
Walk · Mercado 20 de Noviembre → Panteón General de Oaxaca · 1.6 km · 25 min east along Av. Independencia
Panteón General San Miguel — the night of the angelitos
timeline.note: The city's own cemetery: candlelit niches, families sitting with their graves, a municipal cultural programme in the middle, and the Comparsa de Catrinas passing through the centro the same evening. ⚠️ Hours are set by the municipality and change yearly — locals give 'until about 22:00' and 'be there from 20:00 or 21:00'. Go quietly, ask before photographing anyone, and buy your candles and marigolds at the gate.

days.label: Día de Muertos — the market, the hill of graves, the comparsa

walking_km.how: Abastos aisles ~2.0 + Xoxocotlán cemetery ~1.5 + centro ofrenda crawl 2.2 ×1.3 + street 0.6

days.ribbon: Hotel →taxi 15′→ Mercado de Abastos →taxi 25′→ Panteón de Xoxocotlán →taxi 25′→ Alcalá →walk 20′→ centro comparsa
days.rain_alt: The Abastos market, the Museo Textil (free, open until 20:00) and the covered arcades of the Zócalo carry an entire wet day between them; the comparsas run wet or dry.
days.late_cut: cut the Xoxocotlán daytime visit — the ofrendas in the centro and the night comparsa are the parts that do not repeat.

timeline.what: Breakfast · hotel or the Zócalo arcades
Taxi · hotel → Mercado de Abastos · ~2.5 km · 12-20 min · MX$60-90
Mercado de Abastos — the wholesale market on Muertos morning
timeline.price: free to walk; chocolate, mole paste and mezcal by weight
timeline.note: Oaxaca's enormous open market, and on 2 November it is at maximum: whole aisles of cempasúchil and cresta de gallo, mountains of pan de muerto with its little painted faces, mole pastes ground to order, and the chocolate mills grinding cacao with cinnamon while you wait. Go early and keep your bag in front of you — it is a working market, not a promenade.

timeline.what: Taxi · Mercado de Abastos → Panteón de Santa Cruz Xoxocotlán · ~7 km · 20-30 min · MX$150-220
Panteón de Santa Cruz Xoxocotlán, by daylight
timeline.price: free (a donation at the gate is normal)
timeline.note: Xoxo is the most famous of the valley's cemeteries and its nights (31 Oct and 1 Nov) are shoulder-to-shoulder with tour groups. By day on 2 November it is what it is supposed to be: families repainting graves, laying marigold arches, eating beside their dead, brass bands doing the rounds. This is the visit worth planning for.

timeline.what: Breakfast · hotel; the van collects from the centro
Small-group van · Oaxaca → Santa María del Tule · ~12 km · 30-40 min
Árbol del Tule
timeline.note: A 2,000-year-old Montezuma cypress with the stoutest trunk on earth, in a village churchyard. Fifteen minutes is honestly enough, but every tour stops here and it is a pleasant one.

timeline.what: Van · Santa María del Tule → Teotitlán del Valle · ~18 km · 25-35 min
Teotitlán del Valle — a family weaving workshop
timeline.note: The Zapotec rug-weaving village: cochineal ground on a metate in front of you, indigo, pericón and moss dye-pots, and a treadle loom that has been in the same room for four generations. Ask for natural dyes specifically — the aniline rugs are cheaper and look it after a year.

timeline.what: Van · Teotitlán del Valle → Mitla · ~30 km · 40-50 min
Mitla — Zona Arqueológica
timeline.note: The Zapotec/Mixtec funerary centre whose walls are covered in geometric stone mosaic — tens of thousands of cut stones set without mortar, the greca patterns you will recognise from every Oaxacan textile since. The colonial church sits directly on top of one of the palaces, which tells its own story.

timeline.what: Van · Mitla → the palenque on the Hierve el Agua road · ~11 km · 20-30 min

timeline.price: included in most tours; a bottle MX$400–1,500
timeline.note: The palenque is where the agave hearts are roasted in a stone pit, crushed under a horse-drawn tahona and double-distilled in copper — after which the tasting finally makes sense.

brief.visa: German passport = visa-free for tourism up to 180 days; the passport must be valid at least six months and a Personalausweis is not accepted. Arriving by air there is no paper FMM any more — Mexico switched to the digital FMMd, and at AICM adult German biometric passports can use the E-Gates, which print a slip with the entry date and the number of days granted. Photograph that slip; it is your permit. The paid paper tourist card only exists for land crossings, so ignore the websites selling you an 'FMM' for a flight. (Auswärtiges Amt, Reise- und Sicherheitshinweise Mexiko, read 2026-08-15 — re-check before booking.)
brief.holidays: No federal public holiday falls inside 28 Oct – 6 Nov 2026 (date.nager.at, MX 2026: the nearest is Día de la Revolución on 16 November). Día de Muertos itself, 1–2 November, is NOT a statutory rest day — banks and government offices largely work, museums keep normal hours — but it is the single largest cultural mobilisation of the Mexican year: domestic flights, intercity buses and Oaxaca hotels behave like a holiday even though the calendar says otherwise. ⚠️ The CDMX Desfile de Día de Muertos date for 2026 was not published as of 2026-08-15; expect a Saturday (31 Oct or 7 Nov), confirmed 4–6 weeks ahead at cultura.cdmx.gob.mx.
brief.weather: Same dates last year (Open-Meteo archive, 2025-10-28 → 11-06): Mexico City 24 / 10 °C with 0.3 mm of rain across ten days; Oaxaca 26 / 12 °C with none at all. This is the best window of the Mexican year — the rains have stopped and the heat has not started. About 11 h of daylight, sunrise ~07:10 and sunset ~18:00 in CDMX. Two things the averages hide: Mexico City sits at 2,240 m so the first day feels thin and the nights are genuinely cold (a jacket, not a jumper), and Monte Albán at midday has no shade whatsoever.
brief.money: Peso, cash-first outside restaurants and hotels: markets, cemeteries, colectivos, comparsa food stalls, church donations and every tip are cash. Withdraw at bank ATMs (Santander, Banorte, BBVA) rather than the standalone kiosks in tourist streets, and decline the machine's own currency conversion. Cards are fine in Roma Norte and central Oaxaca restaurants. Tipping: 10–15% in restaurants (check whether propina is already on the bill), MX$20–50 for a taxi you liked, MX$50/day housekeeping.
brief.connectivity: eSIM before you fly — Telcel has by far the best coverage in the Oaxacan valleys and most travel eSIMs ride on it; €5–25 pp buys 5–10 GB for ten days. Wi-Fi is good in cafés and hotels in both cities and absent in the cemeteries and at Teotihuacán. Plug type A/B, 127 V — German devices need a plug adapter, and cheap hair dryers do not like the voltage.
brief.insurance: Travel-medical insurance with repatriation cover (Auslandsreise-Kranken- und Rückholversicherung) is the one non-optional purchase. The Auswärtiges Amt states plainly that private hospitals expect payment on the spot in cash and that any consular assistance is billed back to the traveller. €40–90 for two for ten days. Altitude, street food and a lot of mezcal are the three realistic claim causes on this itinerary, in that order.
brief.safety: The Auswärtiges Amt places no blanket travel warning on either Mexico City or the state of Oaxaca (its Oaxaca warning is for the Guatemalan border strip, which this trip never approaches). What the plan does about it rather than warning you: every night block ends in a lit, busy, walkable neighbourhood or a taxi from the door — Roma Norte and the Oaxaca centro both stay awake — and the two cemetery nights are done with the crowd, not after it. Practical: pickpocketing and phone-snatching are the real risks, so a front pocket in the Abastos and Jamaica markets; take authorised sitio taxis or app cars, never a street taxi hailed at the airport (Uber and DiDi have been barred from AICM pickups since March 2026); do not leave a drink unattended in a mezcalería.
brief.baggage: Two checked bags plus cabin. Where the big bag physically is: hotel in Roma Norte on days 2–4 (Teotihuacán and Coyoacán are day trips), flown to Oaxaca on day 5, in the Oaxaca hotel on days 6–8, back to the Roma Norte hotel on day 9, and left at reception on the morning of day 10 while you do the museum. Nothing on this trip needs an overnight bag. Buying mezcal: hold baggage only, 1 L pp duty-free into the EU, and pad the bottle — the Oaxaca market will wrap it in newspaper and call it done.
brief.Día de Muertos playbook: The two cities peak on different nights, which is the whole reason this route works. Mexico City: the Saturday parade on Reforma (date unconfirmed), ofrendas in Coyoacán and Roma Norte, and the cempasúchil canyon at the Mercado de Jamaica in the last week of October. Oaxaca: 1 November is Día de los Angelitos with the Comparsa de Catrinas and the first cemetery vigils, 2 November is the day itself, when the panteones fill from the afternoon and the comparsas escort the souls back after dark. Manners matter more than logistics here: this is a family occasion, not a show. Ask before you photograph anyone, buy your candles and marigolds from the stalls at the cemetery gate, accept the mezcal if it is offered, and do not step over a grave.
